  chain untouched; merging a chain into itself, two chains whose
  parameter shapes or layer order disagree, or an unparseable chain
  structure rejects the whole merge with `ValueError` before one target
  byte is rewritten; an unwritable directory or a full disk raises
  `OSError`. A process killed mid-merge leaves only the old head or the
  new head reachable (both one complete chain), and the residue -- an
  orphan segment beyond the old head -- is reclaimed deterministically
  by the next fork, compaction, deletion or merge.
- `Sequential.verify(source)` verifies an existing incremental checkpoint
  chain (a chain directory or a `MemoryChain`) strictly read-only. It
  walks the basis and every delta through the `head`, checking each
  segment's completeness (framing and CRC), segment order, the basis
  reference and every tensor/layer shape, and returns a success report
  (`ok`, `head`, `segments`) for an intact chain. A truncated segment,
  missing field, out-of-order segment, or a shape/layer-order mismatch
  rejects the **whole** chain with `ValueError` whose message names the
  first bad segment's position and the reason; the chain directory is not
  modified by a single byte (a compaction interrupted on disk is
  inspected in place, not rolled forward). A missing chain directory
  raises `FileNotFoundError`; an operating-system level read failure
  raises `OSError`. `source` may also be a list of chain directories --
  a chain family whose members share prefix segments after a fork. Every
  member is then verified in turn with the same read-only walk, a sound
  family returns a family report (`ok`, `members`, `chains`), and the
  first bad segment across the family is reported with its position, the
  reason and -- for a shared segment -- every chain whose head reaches
  it.

### Threading

All `Sequential` operations are serialised by one per-container lock, so
multiple threads may interleave `forward`, `backward`, `update`,
`adam_step`, `save` and `load`. Under any interleaving each parameter's
final value is one a serial execution of the same calls could have
produced: `update` and `adam_step` each apply as one atomic step, a
`load` is never observed half-applied, and no `save` can read a
half-written tensor (optimizer moments included). Every snapshot
corresponds to one complete slice boundary -- never two passes half
mixed. When two threads save to the same file path the bytes on disk are
always one or the other writer's complete checkpoint (never a blend).

## Checkpoint file semantics

Path saves are atomic: bytes go to a temporary file in the destination
directory, which is `os.replace`d over any existing file (no backup is
kept). A process killed mid-write leaves only the rejected temporary file;
the final path either holds the previous complete checkpoint or the new
one. A half-written or corrupted file at the load path is detected by its
trailer and CRC and refused with `ValueError`.

Floats are stored as raw IEEE-754 float64 values, so a save/load round-trip
is bitwise identical, including the sign of negative zero. Integers must
fit in int64 (the Adam step count included) and all serialized numbers
must be finite; oversized integers or non-finite floats raise
`ValueError` on save -- optimizer moments with such values can never
enter a checkpoint -- and a payload that merely contains an oversized or
non-finite value is refused on load. Saving into a directory that does
not exist or is not writable, or failing because the disk is full,
raises `OSError`; the caller chooses the destination path.

## Checkpoint format versions

The on-disk format is versioned. This build writes **version 3** and
still reads **versions 1 and 2**: an old file is migrated item by item
into the current document shape and the source version is recorded; if
migration fails on any item the whole file is rejected rather than
silently filled in. Version 3 adds the optimizer state (Adam first/second
moments and step count); a version-1 or version-2 checkpoint has no such
state and migrates to `t = 0` with zero moments. A file with an unknown
version, or a header with a field added or removed, is rejected with
`ValueError`. A migrated state re-saves as native version 3. Unknown
(future) versions are never guessed; they are refused.

## Incremental checkpoint chains

Passing an existing directory (or a `MemoryChain`) to `save`/`load` uses an
incremental chain instead of one self-contained file:

- the first save writes a full **basis** segment (`seg-0000000000.seqd`);
- every later save appends a delta segment naming only the tensors that
  changed, compared by encoded leaf identity (so float sign bits such as
  `-0.0` count); unchanged saves append an empty delta deterministically,
  and layers with no parameters participate like any other layer;
- a `head` pointer names the newest committed segment. Each segment file is
  written completely and atomically before the head is advanced, so a crash,
  a full disk or two saves racing into one directory always leave a single
  complete chain reachable from `head`. A training process killed at any
  point therefore leaves a chain that loads to exactly the last complete
  commit, and continuing from it -- appending deltas or taking full saves
  -- stays bit for bit identical to the uninterrupted run.

`Sequential.compact` (or `checkpoint.compact_chain`) folds the basis and a
prefix of the deltas into one new basis segment in place as a streaming
online compaction; see its entry in the interface list above. The fold
walks and checks segments as it writes the new basis, converts the tail a
segment at a time in the slots the chain already owned, and commits
through a stage-then-publish protocol guarded by a cross-process directory
lock and lease: concurrent saves, loads, verifies and compactions on one
directory are serialised at each step (a live fold is read straight
through rather than waited on), a compaction killed at any point is
completed by the next open, and `head` always points at one complete
chain. Peak disk usage stays within the original chain plus the single
new basis segment.

A whole chain family is compacted in one call too: `Sequential.compact`
(or `checkpoint.compact_family`) takes the sequence of member chain
directories and folds the prefix segments every member reaches through
the same shared files (the hard-linked fork prefix) into one new basis
segment stored once and shared by every member. Each member's head is
advanced to that new history while the tail segments it alone owned
follow the new basis in their original order, so the state every member
reassembles -- parameters, gradients, optimizer state and hidden state
-- is bit for bit unchanged and no member's optimizer step moves. The
segment count drops deterministically by exactly the folded range,
repeating the same family fold is a no-op, and a family with no
foldable prefix is left as it was. Each member runs the same streaming,
crash-safe fold a single-chain compaction uses (saves, loads and
incremental appends keep flowing and no member is ever observed as half
a chain); the family fold is serialised against single-chain
compactions, forks, merges and deletions by the directory locks and
leases. Hard-killed mid-fold, each member still loads one complete
state -- its own interrupted fold rolls forward on the next open -- and
the next family operation finishes the fold and reclaims the residue,
neither deleting a reachable shared segment nor leaking an unreachable
one. `checkpoint.compact_family_memory` provides the same family fold for
`MemoryChain` stores.

`Sequential.fork` (or `checkpoint.fork_chain`) turns one chain into a
chain family: the branch directory shares the segments up to the fork
point with the source chain (hard links, so the prefix is stored once)
and then grows its own tail under its own `head`. Every chain of the
family saves, loads, compacts and verifies independently; a shared
segment's bytes are reclaimed exactly when no chain's head can reach it
any more. `Sequential.delete` (or `checkpoint.delete_chain`) removes one
branch of the family -- its directory, its head and the segments it
alone owned -- atomically with respect to concurrent forks and
compactions, and deterministically sweeps crash residue (staging
directories of killed forks/deletes, segments no head can reach) on
every fork, compaction, deletion and merge. `Sequential.merge` (or
`checkpoint.merge_chains`) lands one chain's current state onto another
inside the family: the target keeps all of its segments and gains one
target-owned delta carrying only the genuine difference from the
source, so the target then loads to the source's state bit for bit
while the source is untouched and the shared prefix is stored once;
the merge uses the same segment-then-head append commit a save does,
so a kill leaves only the old or the new head and its orphan residue
is swept on the next family operation. `checkpoint.verify_chain` (or
`Sequential.verify`) accepts a list of chain directories to verify a
whole family read-only, reporting the first bad segment with every chain
that reaches it.

Loading walks the basis and every delta up to the head and reassembles the
state by layer (parameters, gradients, optimizer moments and step count,
then hidden slots). The reassembled state is bit for bit identical to
the full snapshot taken at the same moment, including a chain written by
the previous version-2 engine: old deltas are read, their hidden indices
remapped, and the missing optimizer state filled in from the starting
values. Any segment in the chain that is truncated, corrupt, missing a
field, out of order, changes the layer order or parameter/shapes, or
introduces hidden state incompletely makes the load reject the **whole**
chain with `ValueError`. A missing chain directory or a referenced
segment file that is absent raises `FileNotFoundError`; an unwritable
directory or a full disk raises `OSError`. A chain cannot change the
model's layer order or parameter shapes -- use a fresh full snapshot for
a different model.

`MemoryChain` (exported from `sequence_engine`) is an in-memory chain with
identical commit semantics, useful for tests and long-running processes that
want incremental snapshots without files.

## Tests

    python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .

## Limits

CPU only; no GPU backend.
One backward pass per forward pass.
The engine trains nothing on its own and ships no dataset.

367	            if exc.errno in (errno.EWOULDBLOCK, errno.EAGAIN, errno.EACCES):
368	                return True
369	            return False
370	        try:
371	            fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_UN)
372	        except OSError:
373	            pass
374	        return False
375	    finally:
376	        os.close(fd)

379	def _try_family_lease(parent):
380	    """Take the cross-process family lease non-blockingly.
381	
382	    Returns the locked fd, ``None`` when another live process holds it,
383	    or ``False`` on platforms without ``fcntl`` (the directory and
384	    in-process locks then provide best-effort exclusion).
385	    """
386	    if fcntl is None:
387	        return False
388	    path = _family_lease_path(parent)
389	    fd = os.open(path, os.O_RDWR | os.O_CREAT, 0o644)
390	    try:
391	        fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_EX | fcntl.LOCK_NB)
392	    except OSError as exc:
393	        os.close(fd)
394	        if exc.errno in (errno.EWOULDBLOCK, errno.EAGAIN, errno.EACCES):
395	            return None
396	        raise
397	    return fd

401	    if not fd:
402	        return
403	    try:
404	        fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_UN)
405	    except OSError:
406	        pass
407	    os.close(fd)

410	def _wait_for_family_lease(parent):
411	    """Block until any live family operation over *parent* has ended."""
412	    if not _family_lease_live(parent):
413	        return
414	    if fcntl is None or _family_active_in_process(parent):
415	        while _family_active_in_process(parent):
416	            with _family_dir_lock(parent):
417	                pass
418	            if _family_active_in_process(parent):
419	                time.sleep(0.0)
420	        return
421	    try:
422	        fd = os.open(_family_lease_path(parent), os.O_RDONLY)
423	    except FileNotFoundError:
424	        return
425	    try:
426	        fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_EX)
427	        try:
428	            fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_UN)
429	        except OSError:
430	            pass
431	    finally:
432	        os.close(fd)

435	class _FamilyFoldGuard:
436	    """Serialise a single-chain fold with family folds in the same parent.
437	
438	    Saves, loads, verifies, forks, merges and deletions do not take this
439	    guard -- only a fold (single-chain or family) does -- so ordinary
440	    chain traffic keeps flowing while maintenance folds serialise: a
441	    family fold blocks here until any single-chain fold of a sibling
442	    member finishes, and a single-chain fold blocks while a family fold
443	    is active.  On platforms without ``fcntl`` the in-process family lock
444	    provides the same guarantee within the process.
445	    """
446	
447	    def __init__(self, chain_directory):
448	        self._parent = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(chain_directory))
449	        self._fd = None
450	        self._thread_lock = None
451	
452	    def __enter__(self):
453	        if fcntl is None:
454	            self._thread_lock = _family_dir_lock(self._parent)
455	            self._thread_lock.acquire()
456	            return self
457	        fd = os.open(_family_lease_path(self._parent), os.O_RDWR | os.O_CREAT, 0o644)
458	        try:
459	            # Blocking: wait out any family fold (or another single-chain
460	            # fold of a sibling) instead of spinning.  flock serialises
461	            # separate opens even within one process.
462	            fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_EX)
463	        except BaseException:
464	            os.close(fd)
465	            raise
466	        self._fd = fd
467	        return self
468	
469	    def __exit__(self, *exc_info):
470	        if self._fd is not None:
471	            fd = self._fd
472	            self._fd = None
473	            try:
474	                fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_UN)
475	            except OSError:
476	                pass
477	            os.close(fd)
478	            # Reclaim the lease file when no fold still uses it (a live
479	            # family fold always keeps its marker): the flock above is
480	            # released by close, so an unheld file here is only debris.
481	            if not os.path.exists(_family_marker_path(self._parent)):
482	                path = _family_lease_path(self._parent)
483	                try:
484	                    probe = os.open(path, os.O_RDONLY)
485	                    try:
486	                        try:
487	                            fcntl.flock(probe, fcntl.LOCK_EX | fcntl.LOCK_NB)
488	                        except OSError:
489	                            pass
490	                        else:
491	                            os.unlink(path)
492	                        try:
493	                            fcntl.flock(probe, fcntl.LOCK_UN)
494	                        except OSError:
495	                            pass
496	                    finally:
497	                        os.close(probe)
498	                except OSError:
499	                    pass
500	        if self._thread_lock is not None:
501	            self._thread_lock.release()
502	            self._thread_lock = None
503	        return False

607	def _freeze_tree(tree, shape, payload):
608	    if shape:
609	        if not isinstance(tree, list) or len(tree) != shape[0]:
610	            raise CheckpointError("tensor tree does not match its declared shape")

649	    """Return ``(t, m_entries, v_entries)`` for a document's optimizer state.

678	def _freeze(document):
679	    if not isinstance(document, dict):
680	        raise CheckpointError("checkpoint document must be an object")
681	    missing = _DOCUMENT_KEYS - document.keys()
682	    extra = document.keys() - (_DOCUMENT_KEYS | {"optim"})
683	    if missing or extra:

685	            f"checkpoint document must be an object with the fields "
686	            f"{sorted(_DOCUMENT_KEYS)} (plus an optional 'optim')"
687	        )
688	    payload = []
689	
690	    entries = document.get("params")
691	    if not isinstance(entries, list):
692	        raise CheckpointError("checkpoint must record a parameter tensor list")
693	    param_shapes = [_freeze_entry(entry, payload) for entry in entries]
694	
695	    grads = document.get("grads")
696	    if not isinstance(grads, list) or len(grads) != len(entries):
697	        raise CheckpointError("checkpoint must record one gradient slot per parameter")
698	    grad_shapes = [_freeze_entry(entry, payload) for entry in grads]
699	    if grad_shapes != param_shapes:
700	        raise CheckpointError("parameter and gradient shapes must match")
701	
702	    hidden = document.get("hidden")
703	    if hidden is None:
704	        hidden_shapes = None
705	    else:
706	        if not isinstance(hidden, list) or not hidden:
707	            raise CheckpointError("hidden state must be a non-empty list or null")
708	        hidden_shapes = [_freeze_entry(entry, payload) for entry in hidden]
709	
710	    optim_t, optim_m, optim_v = _resolve_optim(document, param_shapes)
711	    m_shapes = [_freeze_entry(entry, payload) for entry in optim_m]
712	    v_shapes = [_freeze_entry(entry, payload) for entry in optim_v]
713	    if m_shapes != param_shapes or v_shapes != param_shapes:
714	        raise CheckpointError("optimizer moment shapes must match the parameters")
715	
716	    layers = document.get("layers")
717	    if not isinstance(layers, list) or not layers:
718	        raise CheckpointError("checkpoint must record the layer order")
719	    header_layers = [_freeze_layer(layer) for layer in layers]
720	    if sum(len(layer["shapes"]) for layer in header_layers) != len(entries):
721	        raise CheckpointError("layer parameter counts do not match the parameter list")
722	
723	    pending = document.get("pending")
724	    if not isinstance(pending, bool):
725	        raise CheckpointError("pending flag must be a boolean")
726	
727	    header = {
728	        "v": FORMAT_VERSION,
729	        "params": param_shapes,
730	        "grads": grad_shapes,
731	        "hidden": hidden_shapes,
732	        "optim": {"t": optim_t, "m": m_shapes, "v": v_shapes},
733	        "layers": header_layers,
734	        "pending": pending,
735	    }
736	    _exact_keys(header, _FULL_HEADER_KEYS, "checkpoint header")
737	    return header, payload

740	def build_bytes(document):
741	    """Serialize a full snapshot document to the fixed binary representation."""
742	    header, payload = _freeze(document)
743	    return _frame(MAGIC, END_MAGIC, header, payload)

746	def _frame(magic, end_magic, header, payload):
747	    header_bytes = json.dumps(
748	        header, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":"), sort_keys=True
749	    ).encode("utf-8")
750	
751	    body = bytearray()
752	    body += magic
753	    body += struct.pack("<I", header["v"])
754	    body += struct.pack("<Q", len(header_bytes))
755	    body += header_bytes
756	    crc = zlib.crc32(header_bytes)
757	    leaf_count = 0
758	    for chunk in payload:
759	        body += chunk
760	        crc = zlib.crc32(chunk, crc)
761	        leaf_count += 1
762	    body += end_magic
763	    body += struct.pack("<Q", leaf_count)
764	    body += struct.pack("<I", crc & 0xFFFFFFFF)
765	    return bytes(body)

773	class _LeafReader:
774	    def __init__(self, payload):
775	        self._payload = payload
776	        self._pos = 0
777	
778	    def _leaf(self):
779	        tag = self._payload[self._pos]
780	        chunk = self._payload[self._pos + 1 : self._pos + 9]
781	        self._pos += 9
782	        if tag == _TAG_INT:
783	            value = struct.unpack("<q", chunk)[0]
784	            return value
785	        if tag == _TAG_FLOAT:
786	            value = struct.unpack("<d", chunk)[0]
787	            if not math.isfinite(value):
788	                raise CheckpointError(
789	                    "checkpoint payload contains a non-finite floating value"
790	                )
791	            return value
792	        raise CheckpointError(f"unknown leaf tag {tag!r} in payload")
793	
794	    def tree(self, shape):
795	        if not shape:
796	            return self._leaf()
797	        return [self.tree(shape[1:]) for _ in range(shape[0])]
798	
799	    def remaining(self):
800	        return (len(self._payload) - self._pos) // 9

803	def _read_frame(data, magic, end_magic, what):
804	    prefix_len = len(magic) + 4 + 8
805	    if len(data) < prefix_len:
806	        raise CheckpointError(f"{what} is truncated while reading its header")
807	    if data[: len(magic)] != magic:
808	        raise CheckpointError(f"not a {what} (bad magic)")
809	    (version,) = struct.unpack("<I", data[len(magic) : len(magic) + 4])
810	    (header_len,) = struct.unpack(
811	        "<Q", data[len(magic) + 4 : len(magic) + 4 + 8]
812	    )
813	    if header_len <= 0:
814	        raise CheckpointError(f"{what} header length is invalid")
815	
816	    trailer_pos = data.rfind(end_magic)
817	    trailer_len = len(end_magic) + 8 + 4
818	    if trailer_pos < 0 or len(data) - trailer_pos != trailer_len:
819	        raise CheckpointError(f"{what} trailer is missing or the file is torn")
820	    header_start = prefix_len
821	    payload_end = trailer_pos
822	    if header_len > payload_end - header_start:
823	        raise CheckpointError(f"{what} header overruns the payload area")
824	    header_bytes = data[header_start : header_start + header_len]
825	
826	    (leaf_count, stored_crc) = struct.unpack(
827	        "<QI", data[trailer_pos + len(end_magic) :]
828	    )
829	    actual_crc = zlib.crc32(data[header_start:payload_end])
830	    if actual_crc != stored_crc:
831	        raise CheckpointError(f"{what} CRC mismatch: the file is corrupt or torn")
832	
833	    try:
834	        header = json.loads(header_bytes.decode("utf-8"))
835	    except (UnicodeDecodeError, json.JSONDecodeError) as exc:
836	        raise CheckpointError(f"{what} header is invalid: {exc}") from exc
837	    if not isinstance(header, dict):
838	        raise CheckpointError(f"{what} header must be a JSON object")
839	    if header.get("v") != version:
840	        raise CheckpointError(f"{what} header version does not match its frame")
841	
842	    payload = data[header_start + header_len : payload_end]
843	    if len(payload) != leaf_count * 9:
844	        raise CheckpointError(f"{what} payload has the wrong size")
845	    return version, header, payload, leaf_count

907	def parse_bytes(raw):
908	    """Validate and decode a full snapshot (v1, v2 or v3); return the document.
909	
910	    A version-1 or version-2 file is migrated item by item into the current
911	    document shape (a missing optimizer state starts at ``t = 0`` with zero
912	    moments).  Any failure while migrating rejects the whole file -- nothing
913	    is partially returned or filled in.  The document itself carries no
914	    source-version field; use :func:`load_bytes_with_source` when the
915	    originating format version is needed.
916	    """
917	    document, _source = _decode_full(raw)
918	    return document

921	def load_bytes_with_source(source):
922	    """Like :func:`load_bytes`, also returning the source format version."""
923	    if isinstance(source, MemoryChain):
924	        document = load_chain_memory(source)
925	        return document, FORMAT_VERSION
926	    if isinstance(source, (str, os.PathLike)):
927	        path = os.fspath(source)
928	        if os.path.isdir(path):
929	            return load_chain(path), FORMAT_VERSION
930	        with open(path, "rb") as fh:
931	            raw = fh.read()
932	        return _decode_full(raw)
933	    if isinstance(source, (bytes, bytearray, memoryview)):
934	        return _decode_full(source)
935	    raise TypeError("load source must be a path or bytes")

938	def _decode_full(raw):
939	    """Return ``(document, source_version)`` for one full snapshot."""
940	    if not isinstance(raw, (bytes, bytearray, memoryview)):
941	        raise CheckpointError("checkpoint must be bytes")
942	    data = bytes(raw)
943	    version, header, payload, leaf_count = _read_frame(
944	        data, MAGIC, END_MAGIC, "checkpoint"
945	    )
946	    if version not in SUPPORTED_READ_VERSIONS:
947	        raise CheckpointError(
948	            f"unsupported checkpoint version {version}; this build reads "

999	def _migrate_v1_document(document):
1000	    """Migrate a decoded version-1 document item by item.
1001	
1002	    The tensor semantics are shared across versions, so migration is a
1003	    field-by-field re-validation rather than a guess: every tensor, shape
1004	    and descriptor is copied and checked individually.  A failure on any
1005	    item raises and the caller rejects the whole file.  The optimizer
1006	    state, absent before version 3, is filled in separately by
1007	    :func:`_migrate_add_optim`.
1008	    """
1009	    if not isinstance(document, dict):
1010	        raise CheckpointError("v1 checkpoint is not a valid document")
1011	    migrated = {}
1012	    try:
1013	        params = document["params"]
1014	        grads = document["grads"]
1015	        hidden = document["hidden"]
1016	        layers = document["layers"]
1017	        pending = document["pending"]
1018	    except KeyError as exc:
1019	        raise CheckpointError(
1020	            f"v1 checkpoint is missing field {exc.args[0]!r}; refusing to migrate"
1021	        ) from None
1022	    if not isinstance(params, list) or not isinstance(grads, list):
1023	        raise CheckpointError("v1 checkpoint tensor lists are malformed")
1024	    if len(params) != len(grads):
1025	        raise CheckpointError("v1 checkpoint param/gradient counts disagree")
1026	    m_params = []
1027	    m_grads = []
1028	    for index, (p_entry, g_entry) in enumerate(zip(params, grads)):
1029	        m_params.append(_migrate_v1_entry(p_entry, f"parameter {index}"))
1030	        m_grads.append(_migrate_v1_entry(g_entry, f"gradient {index}"))

1032	            raise CheckpointError(
1033	                f"v1 parameter {index} and its gradient disagree on shape"
1034	            )
1035	    migrated["params"] = m_params
1036	    migrated["grads"] = m_grads
1037	    if hidden is None:
1038	        migrated["hidden"] = None
1039	    else:
1040	        if not isinstance(hidden, list) or not hidden:
1041	            raise CheckpointError("v1 hidden state must be a non-empty list or null")
1042	        migrated["hidden"] = [
1043	            _migrate_v1_entry(entry, f"hidden slot {index}")
1044	            for index, entry in enumerate(hidden)
1045	        ]
1046	    if not isinstance(layers, list) or not layers:
1047	        raise CheckpointError("v1 checkpoint must record the layer order")
1048	    m_layers = []
1049	    for index, layer in enumerate(layers):
1050	        _exact_keys(layer, _LAYER_KEYS, f"v1 layer {index} descriptor")
1051	        kind = layer["kind"]
1052	        if not isinstance(kind, str) or not kind:
1053	            raise CheckpointError(f"v1 layer {index} kind must be a non-empty string")
1054	        shapes = layer["shapes"]
1055	        if not isinstance(shapes, list):
1056	            raise CheckpointError(f"v1 layer {index} shapes must be a list")
1057	        m_shapes = []
1058	        for shape in shapes:
1059	            _check_shape(shape)
1060	            m_shapes.append(list(shape))
1061	        m_layers.append({"kind": kind, "shapes": m_shapes})

1063	    if not isinstance(pending, bool):
1064	        raise CheckpointError("v1 pending flag must be a boolean")

1165	def _freeze_delta(document, schema_shapes):
1166	    """Build delta framing from ``{b,n,hc,changed,pending}``.
1167	
1168	    *schema_shapes* maps the flat tensor index of every tensor the
1169	    post-delta state may contain to its shape: params then grads then the
1170	    (newly introduced, if any) hidden slots.
1171	    """
1172	    if not isinstance(document, dict):
1173	        raise CheckpointError("delta document must be an object")
1174	    _exact_keys(document, _DELTA_HEADER_KEYS, "delta header")
1175	    if document["v"] != FORMAT_VERSION:
1176	        raise CheckpointError("delta version must be the current format version")
1177	    basis_name = document["b"]
1178	    if not isinstance(basis_name, str) or basis_name != _segment_name(_BASIS_INDEX):
1179	        raise CheckpointError("delta must name its basis segment")
1180	    number = document["n"]
1181	    if isinstance(number, bool) or not isinstance(number, int) or number <= 0:
1182	        raise CheckpointError("delta segment number must be a positive int")
1183	    hc = document["hc"]
1184	    if hc is not None and (isinstance(hc, bool) or not isinstance(hc, int) or hc < 0):
1185	        raise CheckpointError("delta hidden count must be a non-negative int or null")
1186	    changed = document["changed"]
1187	    if not isinstance(changed, list):
1188	        raise CheckpointError("delta changed list must be a list")
1189	    if not isinstance(document["pending"], bool):
1190	        raise CheckpointError("pending flag must be a boolean")
1191	
1192	    payload = []
1193	    seen = set()
1194	    header_entries = []
1195	    previous_index = -1
1196	    for position, entry in enumerate(changed):
1197	        _exact_keys(entry, _CHANGED_INPUT_KEYS, f"delta changed entry {position}")
1198	        index = entry["i"]
1199	        if isinstance(index, bool) or not isinstance(index, int) or index < 0:
1200	            raise CheckpointError(f"delta changed entry {position} has a bad index")
1201	        if index in seen:
1202	            raise CheckpointError(f"delta lists tensor {index} more than once")
1203	        if index <= previous_index:
1204	            raise CheckpointError("delta changed entries must be strictly ordered")
1205	        previous_index = index
1206	        seen.add(index)
1207	        shape = entry["s"]
1208	        _check_shape(shape)
1209	        if index >= len(schema_shapes):
1210	            raise CheckpointError(
1211	                f"delta changed entry {position} names a tensor beyond the model"
1212	            )
1213	        if list(shape) != schema_shapes[index]:
1214	            raise CheckpointError(
1215	                f"delta changed entry {position} shape does not match the chain"
1216	            )

1218	        if not _shape_matches(tree, shape):
1219	            raise CheckpointError("delta tensor tree does not match its declared shape")

1221	        header_entries.append({"i": index, "s": list(shape)})

1223	    header = {
1224	        "v": FORMAT_VERSION,
1225	        "b": basis_name,
1226	        "n": number,
1227	        "hc": hc,
1228	        "changed": header_entries,
1229	        "pending": document["pending"],

1234	def _parse_delta(raw, segment_index_expected):
1235	    """Validate one delta segment and return ``(number, hc, pending, items)``.
1236	
1237	    *items* is a list of ``(flat_index, shape, tree)`` already decoded.
1238	    """
1239	    if not isinstance(raw, (bytes, bytearray, memoryview)):
1240	        raise CheckpointError("delta segment must be bytes")

1242	        bytes(raw), DELTA_MAGIC, DELTA_END_MAGIC, "delta segment"
1243	    )
1244	    if version not in SUPPORTED_DELTA_VERSIONS:
1245	        raise CheckpointError(
1246	            f"delta segments must be version {SUPPORTED_DELTA_VERSIONS}, "
1247	            f"got {version}"
1248	        )
1249	    _exact_keys(header, _DELTA_HEADER_KEYS, "delta header")
1250	    if header["v"] != version:
1251	        raise CheckpointError("delta header version does not match")
1252	    if header["b"] != _segment_name(_BASIS_INDEX):
1253	        raise CheckpointError("delta does not name the chain's basis segment")
1254	    number = header["n"]
1255	    if isinstance(number, bool) or not isinstance(number, int) or number <= 0:
1256	        raise CheckpointError("delta segment number must be a positive int")
1257	    if number != segment_index_expected:
1258	        raise CheckpointError(
1259	            f"delta segment number {number} does not match its position "
1260	            f"{segment_index_expected} in the chain"
1261	        )
1262	    hc = header["hc"]
1263	    if hc is not None and (isinstance(hc, bool) or not isinstance(hc, int) or hc < 0):
1264	        raise CheckpointError("delta hidden count must be a non-negative int or null")
1265	    changed = header["changed"]
1266	    if not isinstance(changed, list):
1267	        raise CheckpointError("delta changed list must be a list")
1268	    if not isinstance(header["pending"], bool):
1269	        raise CheckpointError("pending flag must be a boolean")
1270	
1271	    total_leaves = 0
1272	    seen = set()
1273	    descriptors = []
1274	    previous_index = -1
1275	    for position, entry in enumerate(changed):
1276	        _exact_keys(entry, _CHANGED_KEYS, f"delta changed entry {position}")
1277	        index = entry["i"]
1278	        if isinstance(index, bool) or not isinstance(index, int) or index < 0:
1279	            raise CheckpointError(f"delta changed entry {position} has a bad index")
1280	        if index in seen or index <= previous_index:
1281	            raise CheckpointError(
1282	                f"delta changed entry {position} is duplicated or out of order"
1283	            )
1284	        seen.add(index)
1285	        previous_index = index
1286	        shape = entry["s"]
1287	        _check_shape(shape)
1288	        total_leaves += _shape_size(shape)
1289	        descriptors.append((index, list(shape)))
1290	    if total_leaves != leaf_count:
1291	        raise CheckpointError("delta leaf count does not match its changed tensors")
1292	
1293	    reader = _LeafReader(payload)
1294	    items = [
1295	        (index, shape, reader.tree(shape)) for index, shape in descriptors
1296	    ]
1297	    if reader.remaining() != 0:
1298	        raise CheckpointError("delta payload has trailing bytes")

1307	def _tensors_from_document(document):
1308	    """Return ``{flat_index: (shape, tree)}`` for one full state document.
1309	
1310	    The flat index space is: parameters, gradients, optimizer first
1311	    moments, optimizer second moments, the optimizer step count (a scalar),
1312	    then the hidden slots.  Hidden slots come last so introducing hidden
1313	    state mid-chain only ever appends new indices.
1314	    """
1315	    tensors = {}
1316	    offset = 0
1317	    for entry in document["params"]:
1318	        tensors[offset] = (entry["s"], entry["v"])
1319	        offset += 1
1320	    for entry in document["grads"]:
1321	        tensors[offset] = (entry["s"], entry["v"])
1322	        offset += 1
1323	    optim = document["optim"]
1324	    for entry in optim["m"]:
1325	        tensors[offset] = (entry["s"], entry["v"])
1326	        offset += 1
1327	    for entry in optim["v"]:
1328	        tensors[offset] = (entry["s"], entry["v"])
1329	        offset += 1
1330	    tensors[offset] = ([], optim["t"])
1331	    offset += 1
1332	    hidden = document["hidden"]
1333	    if hidden is not None:
1334	        for entry in hidden:
1335	            tensors[offset] = (entry["s"], entry["v"])
1336	            offset += 1
1337	    return tensors

1345	def _trees_differ(a, b, shape):
1346	    if shape:
1347	        if not isinstance(a, list) or not isinstance(b, list):
1348	            return True
1349	        if len(a) != shape[0] or len(b) != shape[0]:
1350	            return True
1351	        return any(
1352	            _trees_differ(x, y, shape[1:]) for x, y in zip(a, b)

1359	def _assemble(basis_document, applied):
1360	    """Build a full document from basis tensors plus per-index replacements.
1361	
1362	    *applied* maps a flat tensor index (params, grads, optimizer moments,
1363	    step count, then hidden) to ``(shape, tree)``.  Hidden indices only
1364	    exist once a delta introduced hidden state; a complete set must be
1365	    present at that point.
1366	    """
1367	    param_count = len(basis_document["params"])
1368	    layers = basis_document["layers"]
1369	    hidden_count = len(basis_document["hidden"]) if basis_document["hidden"] is not None else None
1370	
1371	    # The latest delta in the chain decides whether hidden state exists.
1372	    final_hidden_count = applied.get("_hc", hidden_count)
1373	    tensors = applied["tensors"]
1374	
1375	    hidden_base = _flat_hidden_base(param_count)
1376	    total = hidden_base + (final_hidden_count or 0)
1377	    for index in range(total):
1378	        if index not in tensors:
1379	            raise CheckpointError(
1380	                f"chain is missing tensor {index}: the delta chain is incomplete"
1381	            )
1382	
1383	    def entries(start, stop):
1384	        return [
1385	            {"s": list(tensors[i][0]), "v": tensors[i][1]}
1386	            for i in range(start, stop)
1387	        ]
1388	
1389	    params = entries(0, param_count)
1390	    grads = entries(param_count, 2 * param_count)
1391	    optim_m = entries(2 * param_count, 3 * param_count)
1392	    optim_v = entries(3 * param_count, 4 * param_count)
1393	    step_shape, step_count = tensors[4 * param_count]
1394	    if step_shape != []:
1395	        raise CheckpointError("optimizer step count tensor must be a scalar")

1399	    if len(params) != param_count or len(grads) != param_count:
1400	        raise CheckpointError("chain did not preserve the parameter/gradient count")

1402	        "params": params,
1403	        "grads": grads,
1404	        "hidden": hidden if final_hidden_count is not None else None,
1405	        "optim": {"t": step_count, "m": optim_m, "v": optim_v},
1406	        "layers": layers,
1407	        "pending": applied["pending"],

1464	class _DirectoryChainLock:
1465	    """Mutual exclusion for one chain directory, in-process and across
1466	    processes.
1467	
1468	    The per-process threading lock serialises this process; an advisory
1469	    ``flock`` on the directory's own file descriptor serialises
1470	    cooperating processes (no extra lock file is created, so a chain
1471	    directory never gains visible entries).  Where the directory cannot
1472	    be locked -- a platform without ``fcntl``, or a filesystem that
1473	    refuses the lock -- the in-process lock alone is used.  Every
1474	    directory-chain operation (save, load, compact) runs entirely under
1475	    this lock, so a reader never observes a half-committed chain and a
1476	    compaction never races a save.
1477	    """
1478	
1479	    def __init__(self, directory):
1480	        self._directory = directory
1481	        self._thread_lock = _chain_lock(directory)
1482	        self._fd = None
1483	
1484	    def __enter__(self):
1485	        self._thread_lock.acquire()
1486	        if fcntl is not None:
1487	            try:
1488	                fd = os.open(
1489	                    self._directory,
1490	                    os.O_RDONLY | getattr(os, "O_DIRECTORY", 0),
1491	                )
1492	            except FileNotFoundError:
1493	                # The directory was deleted (renamed aside by a branch
1494	                # delete) between the caller's existence check and the
1495	                # lock: report the documented missing-directory error
1496	                # rather than degrading to a headless chain.
1497	                self._thread_lock.release()
1498	                raise
1499	            except OSError:
1500	                fd = None
1501	            if fd is not None:
1502	                try:
1503	                    fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_EX)
1504	                except OSError:
